agent.definition: A model that is called in a loop, asks for tools, and is stopped by the code around it. The model is one part of the agent.

agent-loop.definition: The code that calls the model, runs the tools the model asks for, adds the results to the history, and calls the model again. It stops when one of its exits is taken.

context-window.definition: The fixed-size desk the model reads on each call. Instructions, earlier messages, tool results and the reply all share it.

conversation-history.definition: The earlier messages in the list. The harness keeps them, and decides how much of them each call sends.

coroutine.definition: What an async def function returns when you call it.

dataclass.definition: A Python class that holds named fields. The @dataclass decorator writes the __init__ method, so Rein can build a reply with named fields.

done-claim.definition: The model's own statement that it has finished, carried by end_turn. The loop treats it as a claim to check. It is not proof that the task is done.

exit.definition: A reason the loop stops. A loop with one exit stops only when that one exit is taken.

failure-family.definition: A named kind of failure that recurs across runs, such as a false done. Each module teaches one family.

hallucination.definition: A fluent, specific claim that is false. The reply reads the same as a true one, so reading it does not reveal the error.

harness.definition: Everything around the model: the loop, the tools, the permissions, the checks and the limits. Same model, different harness, different results.

harness-board.definition: The harness's settings, such as limits and gates, shown next to what a run does.

inference.definition: A model call that reads the weights and the prompt and produces a reply. The weights stay the same during inference.

input-tokens.definition: The tokens the model reads on a call: the instructions, the earlier messages, the tool results and the new message.

language-model.definition: A model that reads a text and scores the possible next tokens. A harness calls it again and again, and each call gives one reply.

latency.definition: How long a call takes to finish. More tokens in and out usually mean a longer wait.

memory.definition: Anything a run can use later: what is in the window, what is in saved files, or what is in the model's weights.

messages-array.definition: The ordered list of messages sent with each call. It is the conversation the model can see.

model-interface.definition: One function that Rein calls to get a reply. A scripted model and a real model both sit behind it, with the same inputs and the same kind of result.

next-token-prediction.definition: The model's one job on each step: score every possible next token. Nothing in this step checks whether a token is true.

output-limit.definition: The most tokens one reply may use. A reply that reaches it stops there, and the reply says why.

output-tokens.definition: The tokens the model writes in its reply. They use the same window as the input.

pass-rate.definition: The share of trials that pass their checks. It is a measure over many runs, not the result of one.

probability.definition: A number from zero to one that says how likely a choice is. The sampler turns the scores into probabilities before it picks.

react.definition: A name for the loop of reasoning and acting in turns, from the paper ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models.

role.definition: The label on each message in the list. A message is from the user or from the assistant.

run.definition: One agent doing one task, from the first model call to a stop. A run has many turns.

sampling.definition: The step that picks one token from the scored options, by the rules it is given. The model scores; the sampler picks.

seed.definition: The number that sets the random draws of a scripted run. The same seed gives the same run, every time.

stateless.definition: Keeping nothing between calls. A stateless call starts from what it is sent, and nothing else.

system-prompt.definition: The instructions sent with every call, kept apart from the messages. The harness sends it each time.

temperature.definition: A setting of the sampler that changes how much the scores count. Higher temperature spreads the choice over more tokens. At zero, the top token always wins.

token.definition: A piece of text the model reads and writes. A token is often a word, but it can be part of a word or a punctuation mark.

token-budget.definition: A cap on the total tokens a run may use, input and output together. The loop checks it before each call and stops when the total has reached the cap.

tokenizer.definition: The part that cuts text into tokens. Real tokenizers differ, so a count from the course is an estimate.

tool.definition: A function the harness runs when the model asks for it. The model only asks. The harness runs the function and returns the result.

tool-registry.definition: A table from each tool name to the Python function that runs it. The loop looks up the name the model asked for. A name that is not in the table gets an error result.

trace.definition: The record of a run: each model call, reply, permission, tool call and check, in order.

training.definition: The process that sets the model's weights, from many example texts. It happens before any chat, and a chat does not run it.

trial.definition: One run with one seed. A bench runs many trials of the same setup.

turn.definition: One call to the model and the tool results that follow it. A run is a series of turns.

turn-limit.definition: A cap on the number of model calls in one run. When the count reaches it, the loop stops.

type-hint.definition: A note that says what type a name should hold, such as count: int, or -> str after the parameters of a function.

weights.definition: The numbers inside the model that set its scores. Training sets them. Inference only reads them.
